docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
The purpose of this document is to help you effectively use your BCIT email, an essential tool for communication in the CST program. It provides important features such as the benefits of a BCIT email, setting up filters, connecting to an external email client like Microsoft Outlook, and adding a professional signature.

For more information, please visit the official BCIT website.

docs.title: User Demographic
docs.text:
This documentation is targeted towards the following users:

  • Students enrolled in any program at BCIT who want to optimize their BCIT email
  • First-year students new to BCIT's email system

docs.title: Prerequisite Knowledge
docs.text:
The Documentation assumes the following:

  • You already have an active BCIT email account
  • You can use common mouse actions (click, double-click, right-click) and keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl, Alt, Shift)
  • You are familiar with basic email concepts such as inboxes, folders, composing messages, and attachments from using other email services

docs.title: Software Requirements
docs.text: No specialized technical skills are required to follow this guide. You will need a computer running Windows, macOS, or Linux, and access to a modern web browser (such as Chrome, Firefox, Safari, or Edge).

docs.title: Procedures Overview
docs.text:
The main sections of the documentation are summarized below:

  • Setting up external email client
  • Setting up identity
  • Filtering Submission Receipts
  • Signing up for GitHub Education

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Filters automatically sort your incoming emails based on rules you define. For example, moving all emails from a professor into a specific folder.

Guess what? You can now get rid of the Submission Receipt clutter in your inbox! Here are the steps to get started.

docs.title: Accessing myBCIT Email
docs.text:
1. Log into MyBCIT

  2. Click My Mail in the top-right corner.

    ImageGif

docs.title: Opening Settings and Filters
docs.text:
1. In your myBCIT email, click Settings (top-right)

    ImageGif

  2. Under Settings, select Filters.

    ImageGif

docs.title: Creating a New Filter
docs.text:
1. Click + to add a new filter.

    ImageGif

    About roundcube

    roundcube is the default filter set in your myBCIT email. This set is managed by the Roundcube webmail system, which is the standard interface for myBCIT email accounts. So don't worry about it!

  2. Set Filter Name

    ImageGif

docs.title: Configuring Filter Rules
docs.text:
1. Set your condition

    ImageGif

    Filter Condition Types

    • matching all of the following rules: The email must meet every condition (AND)
    • matching any of the following rules: The email meets at least one condition (OR)
    • all messages: Applies to every incoming email, no conditions needed

  2. Under Subject, select From

    ImageGif

  3. Right of contains box, select the text field and insert mail.learn.bcit.ca.

    ImageGif

    Why Use Domain Filtering

    The original address is no-reply@mail.learn.bcit.ca.

    However, using just the domain mail.learn.bcit.ca rather than the full address is more reliable. It'll catch all emails from The Learning Hub regardless of any minor sender variations.

docs.title: Setting Filter Actions
docs.text:
1. Under Inbox, select Archive

    ImageGif

    Warning

    Make sure the Filter disabled toggle in the bottom-right is off so your filter is active.

  2. Once ready, click Save

    ImageGif

Success

Congratulations! You have successfully uncluttered your inbox with one of many filters!

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
By completing this tutorial, you have successfully:

  • ✅ Created a filter in your myBCIT webmail
  • ✅ Set a rule to identify emails from The Learning Hub
  • ✅ Configured an action to automatically move them out of your inbox

You may go onto the next tab to learn how to take advantage of your email!

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: Term Definition BCIT Email Your official email address provided by the British Columbia Institute of Technology (BCIT), typically in the format of @student.bcit.ca or @bcit.ca, used for account verification and student benefits. Cloud Credits Free credits or funds provided by cloud service providers (such as AWS, Azure, or DigitalOcean) as part of the GitHub Student Developer Pack to help students build and deploy applications. Email Signature A customizable block of text automatically added to the end of your emails, typically containing your name, contact information, and professional details. Used to provide a professional appearance to your correspondence. Identity An identity is a kind of profile that contains your name, email address, organization and signature, while also allowing you to set automatic fowarding to different emails. External Email Client / Native Client A desktop or mobile application (such as Microsoft Outlook, Apple Mail, or Mozilla Thunderbird) that allows you to manage and send emails from your BCIT account without using the web-based MyBCIT interface. IMAP Internet Message Access Protocol (IMAP) is a protocol that synchronizes emails by storing messages on a central server instead of storing them locally. SMTP Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) is the standard protocol for sending emails across IP networks. STARTTLS STARTTLS is a security protocol that encrypts plaintext email connections into a secure connection. Filter Rule A specific condition or set of conditions defined within a filter that determines which emails will be automatically processed. For example, filtering emails based on sender, subject line, or keywords. Filter Set A collection of rules (filters) that automatically process your incoming messages based on criteria you define. GitHub Billing Information Your payment and account details on GitHub, including your full legal name and billing address. This must match your academic affiliation documents for successful student status verification. GitHub Classroom A platform integrated with GitHub that allows educators to create assignments and manage student work, enabling educators and students to develop together. GitHub Pro A premium GitHub subscription that includes unlimited public and private repositories, advanced features, and collaboration tools at no cost for verified students. GitHub Student Developer Pack A collection of free tools and services provided by GitHub for students, including GitHub Pro, cloud credits, design software, and more. Available to verify students at educational institutions worldwide. GitHub User Profile Your personal GitHub account page that displays your profile information, including your full name, bio, avatar, and activity history. A complete profile with accurate information is required for student verification. MyBCIT BCIT's web-based student portal that provides access to email, course information, academic records, and other student services. The email component uses the Roundcube webmail system. Student Status Verification The process of confirming your enrollment at an educational institution through GitHub Education, typically using your school email address or student ID documentation. Two-Factor Authentication A security feature that requires two forms of verification (such as a password and a code from your phone) to access your GitHub account, protecting it from unauthorized access. Verified Student A status on GitHub indicating that your student status has been confirmed through your school email address or other official documentation, allowing you to access student benefits and packages.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
An external email client is an email client that is not BCIT Webmail.

By setting up an external email client you can use a service like Microsoft Outlook to view and send emails from your BCIT Account.

You can set up multiple external email clients while still being able to use BCIT Webmail if you so choose.

docs.title: Before you Begin
docs.text:
This walkthrough will be assuming that your external email client of choice is Outlook.

Warning

Gmail will not work for this method of setting up an external client.

docs.title: Enable Native Client
docs.text:
1. Sign in to your BCIT Email in Webmail.

  2. Go to the Settings tab in the top right of the screen.

    Image

  3. Go to the settings section Preferences.

    Image

  4. Go to the Section Native Client.

    Image

    Info

    Native Email clients are programs that handle emails as an standalone software installed on your device, as opposed to Webmail which is all handled in the browser.

  5. Next to Enable Native Client click the slider.

    Image

    Success

    The slider should be blue after you click it.

  6. Click on the Save button.

    Image

docs.title: Configuring Outlook
docs.text:
1. Click the Add account button in Outlook.

    Image

  2. Under the Suggested accounts header, add your BCIT Email, then continue.

    Image

    1. Click the IMAP option in the list.
    GIF

  3. Under the Password header enter your BCIT Email password

    Image

  4. Ensure that the IMAP Incoming server is imap.my.bcit.ca, the Port is 993, and the Secure connection type* is SSL / TLS.

  5. Ensure that your SMTP username is your BCIT Email.

  6. Ensure that the SMTP Outgoing server is smtp.my.bcit.ca and the Port is 587.

    Warning

    These should be the default values. If any of these are not the suggested values, correct them.

    GIF

  7. Under the Secure connection type change the value to StartTLS.

    Warning

    This will not be the default value, make sure to change it.

  8. Press Continue twice.

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
By the end of this guide, you will have successfully:

✅ Enabled usage of external email clients ✅ Set up Outlook as an external email client

While this process is not quite nessasary, if you check your Webmail infrequently or forget to check your Webmail this can grant you easier access to emails sent to you.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
An identity is a kind of profile that contains your name, email address, organization and signature, while also allowing you to set automatic fowarding to different emails.

A signature is a footer automatically placed at the end of every email you send.

docs.title: Add An Identity
docs.text:
1. Sign in to your BCIT Email in Webmail.

  2. Go to the Settings tab in the top right of the screen.

    Image

  3. Go to the settings section Identities.

    Image

  4. Click on the Plus (+) button in the bottom of the screen, underneath the Identities tab.

    Image

docs.title: Adding Information
docs.text:
1. Set your Display Name, your display name should be your real name (i.e. John Doe).
  2. Set your Email, this should be your BCIT email.
  3. Set your Organization (i.e. BCIT).

  4. Click the Set default slider.

    Info

    This will set this identity as the default one used by your emails.

  5. Set your Signature, this will be put at the end of every email. This can be whatever you want it to be, however it should give important information about you, i.e. 

    --
Thanks, John Doe  
CST Set A, Term 1  
A01234567

    Success

    It should look something like this:

    Image

  6. Click on the Save button.

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
By the end of this guide you will have successfully:

✅ Added an identity to be used for your emails ✅ Added a signature to be placed at the end of your emails

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The GitHub Student Developer Pack is a collection of free tools and services provided by GitHub for students. It includes free GitHub Pro, access to educational resources, cloud credits, and more. As a BCIT student, you're eligible to claim these valuable benefits.

Ready to unlock free developer tools? The GitHub Student Developer Pack includes everything from GitHub Pro to cloud credits and design tools!

docs.title: Am I qualified for Github Education?
docs.text:
You qualify for Github Education if you:

  • Are enrolled in a degree- or diploma-granting program, such as a high school, college, university, or homeschool.
  • Have a verifiable school-issued email or documents proving your student status.
  • Own a GitHub personal account.
  • Are at least 13 years old.

docs.title: What documents can I use to prove I'm a student?
docs.text:
• A picture of your school ID with current enrollment date
  • Your class schedule
  • Your transcript
  • An affiliation or enrollment verification letter

docs.title: Preparing Your GitHub Account
docs.text:
1. Go to the GitHub Education website.

    ImageGif

  2. Click Sign in with GitHub if you already have an account, or Sign up to create a new one.

    Creating a New Account

    If you're creating a new account, make sure to use your BCIT email address to verify your student status later.

  3. Complete the GitHub account setup if you're new to the platform.

    Warning

    Make sure you completed your GitHub billing information with your full name exactly as it appears in your academic affiliation document. You do not have to add a payment method. You may need to log out and log back in to GitHub before reapplying. If you have only a single legal name, enter it in both the first and last name fields.

docs.title: Verifying Your Student Status
docs.text:
1. Once logged in, click the Start an application button.

  2. Complete the form.

  3. Select Share Location then press Continue.

    Success

    The Share Location button should look like this if successful

docs.title: Submitting Proof of Enrollment
docs.text:
1. Select your method of verification.

    Acceptance Rates

    How likely each document is to be accepted:

    • Good - Most likely to be accepted
    • Fair - May be accepted
    • Poor - Less likely to be accepted

  2. Upload proof of enrollment, then click Continue

  3. Wait a few days for approval. Make sure to check your BCIT email for an acceptance/rejection email.

Success

Congratulations! Your approval email/status will look like this

docs.title: Unlocking Your Benefits
docs.text:
1. Return to Education Benefits after confirming your email.

  2. Your application type should now show as Student. Explore the available benefits listed on the page.

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
By the end of this guide, you will have successfully:

✅ Created or signed into your GitHub account ✅ Verified your student status with your BCIT email ✅ Unlocked access to the GitHub Student Developer Pack ✅ Gained access to free premium tools and services

The GitHub Student Developer Pack provides incredible value during your time at BCIT. Take advantage of tools like GitHub Pro, cloud credits, design software, and more. These resources will enhance your learning and development skills throughout your studies.

For more information about individual benefits and how to use them, visit the GitHub Education website.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptoms Probable Cause Action Application rejected; message about GitHub account security Your GitHub account does not have two-factor authentication enabled Go to your GitHub account settings, navigate to Security, and enable two-factor authentication. You may need to log out and log back in before reapplying. Application rejected; message about billing information Your GitHub billing information is incomplete or does not match your academic affiliation documents Complete your GitHub billing information with your full legal name exactly as it appears in your academic affiliation document. Ensure the information matches your school records. Log out and log back in before reapplying. Application rejected; message about contributions You don't have enough contributions to GitHub or GitHub Classroom assignments Try applying again after making more contributions to any GitHub Classroom assignments created by your teacher or demonstrating activity on GitHub. Application rejected; message about profile verification Your GitHub user profile is incomplete or inaccurate Complete your GitHub user profile with your full name exactly as it appears in your academic affiliation document. Do not use a variation of your name or a nickname. Log out and log back in before reapplying. Emails from Learning Hub still appearing in inbox Your filter may be disabled, or the domain filter doesn't match the sender address Go to Settings > Filters, verify that your filter is active (toggle is off). Ensure your filter condition uses mail.learn.bcit.ca as the sender address, not the full email address. Filter not catching Learning Hub emails You may have entered the wrong email address or domain in the filter condition Go to Settings > Filters, edit your filter, and verify that you used mail.learn.bcit.ca in the text field, not the full sender address starting with "no-reply@". Can't find archived emails Archived emails are moved out of your inbox but remain in your mailbox Archive folder Check your mailbox folder list on the left side of your email. Look for the Archive folder, or use the Search function to locate your archived messages. Filter applying to all emails instead of just Learning Hub You may have selected the all messages condition instead of creating a specific rule Edit your filter in Settings > Filters. Make sure you selected matching any of the following rules or matching all of the following rules, not all messages. Filter isn't working anymore The Filter disabled toggle may have been accidentally turned on Go to Settings > Filters, select your filter, and verify that the Filter disabled toggle in the bottom-right is off to activate the filter. Multiple filters conflicting with each other You may have multiple filters with overlapping conditions that interfere with each other Go to Settings > Filters and review all your active filters. Check that your filter conditions are specific and don't overlap. You may need to edit or delete conflicting filters.
